core_obligations: Uniqueness: any continuous map P -> Q that extends the vertex restriction of Phi and commutes with the two diagonals satisfies tr = beta_Q^(n) o tr^(2^n) o triangle_P^(n) for every n, hence is unique by continuity (source lines 1200-1202 and 1229-1230).

Existence by induction on dim P: define tr on the (d-1)-skeleton by the induction hypothesis, show with the filtration P(n) = P minus the union of the slabs (k bottom(P) + (2^n-1-k) top(P) + P)/2^n and with cor:DIMENSION that the iterated diagonal of z in P(n) lands in the (d-1)-skeleton so that tr(z) = beta_Q^(n) o (tr|boundary)^(2^n) o triangle_P^(n)(z) is forced, and treat the main axis [bottom(P), top(P)] by the same dichotomy as in dimension one (lines 1211-1230).

Continuity and inversion: prove continuity of that definition at points of the main axis with an explicit epsilon/delta argument splitting non-dyadic and dyadic axis points (choosing n with diam Q < 2^n epsilon), and conclude that tr is an isomorphism of PolySub whose face correspondence agrees with Phi, with inverse tr_Q^P (lines 1232-1271).
proof_roadmap: Introduce the iterated diagonal triangle_P^(n): P -> P^(2^n) and the averaging map beta_P^(n), and note that tr must equal beta_Q^(n) o tr^(2^n) o triangle_P^(n).
Induction on the dimension d: the case d = 0 is trivial and d = 1 is settled by the dyadic dichotomy on [0,1].

For general d, restrict to the (d-1)-skeleton using Lemma:DiagOnFace, then analyse the filtration P(n): faces of the iterated subdivision are either the all-bottom/all-top type (whose beta-image is exactly the removed slabs) or have all codimensions at least one, so z in P(n) has its iterated diagonal on the skeleton.
Handle the main axis by the one-dimensional dichotomy and prove continuity there by choosing n with diam Q < 2^n epsilon and splitting into the two cases of source lines 1236-1267.
Point (2) follows because the inverse morphism in PolySub is the transition map tr_Q^P.
difficulty_reason: The proposition demands a map between two different positively oriented polytopes that simultaneously extends a prescribed vertex bijection and commutes with two different diagonal maps; the proof shows such a tr is forced to be beta_Q^(n) o tr^(2^n) o triangle_P^(n) (source line 1202), so the map has to be manufactured rather than read off. Existence is an induction on the dimension whose induction step needs the filtration P(n) together with cor:DIMENSION to know that the iterated diagonal of z in P(n) lies in the (d-1)-skeleton (lines 1213-1229). The part that cannot be done routinely is continuity at the main axis [bottom(P),top(P)]: it requires a dichotomy between non-dyadic and dyadic axis points and an explicit choice of n with diam Q < 2^n epsilon (lines 1232-1267), a quantitative argument that no standard polytope fact supplies.
